name: Trade war & tariffs
summary: China's rare-earth control pause ends 10 Nov; US tariffs steady
state: China's one-year suspension of its October 2025 rare-earth export controls expires on 10 Nov and no renewal had been announced as of 3 Nov; its April 2025 licensing rules remain in force. US Section 301 tariffs keep the average effective tariff near 7%. No new tariff round was announced on 1–3 Nov.
for_you: Possible price rises and delays for goods using Chinese components; no new tariffs on consumers this week.
rubric_hit: Export-control deadline; tariffs in force = Watch

sources.title: FXStreet — China's rare-earth leverage has an expiration date: 10 Nov

why: Tariffs raise prices, reroute supply chains and slow growth; escalation cycles hurt export-heavy economies like the UK's partners.
drivers: US tariff policy, retaliation, court rulings, trade deals, WTO disputes.

rubric.alert: Broad new tariffs in force with retaliation under way, or US average effective tariff rising sharply.
rubric.watch: New major tariffs announced or threatened between large economies.
rubric.normal: Tariff regime stable; no new major measures in the past two weeks.
